exact_statement: There is one fixed binary 66x66 pattern H such that for every h>=1, with m=2^h, d=386h+2, n=dm, and epsilon=d^-2, a binary n-by-n matrix A_h has dist_H(A_h)>=epsilon and N_H(A_h)/n^132<=epsilon*2^-h. Copies preserve the row and column orders and match both zeros and ones; edits may change entries in either direction.
assumptions: Both row and column indices are selected increasingly
H-freeness is repaired by arbitrary 0-to-1 or 1-to-0 cell changes
novelty_boundary: This is the pinned release theorem itself. Prior work already gives qualitative ordered removal; ternary-host nonpolynomial testing lower bounds were known. No priority claim is made.
costs: The witness has n=(386h+2)2^h and a dense representation takes n^2 bits. Direct materialization writes Theta(n^2) cells. This is a quantitative counterexample family, not an efficient construction claim.
falsifier: An H-free host within fewer than m^2 edits, or an H-copy whose (65,65) pattern entry is outside the claimed diagonal leaf set, would contradict the stated construction bounds.
next_gate: Independent specialist audit of Proposition 3.1 and Lemmas 4.1-4.5 / Proposition 4.6 in the pinned paper; external review and priority remain open.

exact_statement: For A_h above, a tester that independently samples uniform q-element row and column sets and rejects only when their induced ordered submatrix contains H has rejection probability at most epsilon_h*2^-h*q^2. Constant rejection probability rho therefore requires q>=sqrt(rho)*epsilon_h^-1/2*2^(h/2)=exp(Omega(epsilon_h^-1/2)) per axis along the sequence.
assumptions: Canonical induced row/column sampling as specified
Rejection occurs only upon observing an H-copy inside the sample
The pattern H is the fixed 66x66 pattern from claim CA-OAI190-REMOVAL
novelty_boundary: The pinned release includes this canonical-sampler corollary. It does not imply a lower bound for arbitrary adaptive or noncanonical testers.
costs: The required axis sample is q>=sqrt(rho)*epsilon^-1/2*2^((epsilon^-1/2-2)/772). Reading the full induced sample uses q^2 cells; the report does not convert this into a lower bound for other query models.
falsifier: A canonical sampler with smaller q and constant rejection probability on the source matrices would violate the union-bound consequence.
next_gate: Keep arbitrary adaptive tester complexity as UNKNOWN unless a distributional indistinguishability construction is separately proved.

exact_statement: For each source host A_h, the set L_h of m=2^h diagonal leaf cells intersects every original H-copy. Changing all these m entries from 1 to 0 destroys each original copy, but an explicit W+ configuration creates a new copy. Any H-free repair still requires at least m^2=4^h edits, so this old-copy hitting set is smaller than a full repair by a factor at least m.
assumptions: Ordered induced copies matching zeros and ones
The universal copy-location and distance claims from the pinned release theorem
novelty_boundary: The release explicitly notes that editing the old-copy hitting set creates new copies. This report derives the repair-to-hitting ratio from that example and the distance bound; no independent novelty claim is made.
costs: The finite verifier builds dense hosts for h=1 (776x776) and h=2 (3096x3096); it verifies selected copies, not all-copy enumeration or all-edit search.
falsifier: If zeroing the full L_h set did not create the specified W+ copy, or if an all-copy hitting set of size m were already a full repair, the stated adversarial distinction would fail.
next_gate: Independent proof review of universal copy localization and exact body-role indexing; finite h checks are not a substitute.
